body.description: Use case: stylized-concept. STYLE TAKES PRIORITY: STRICT early handheld segmented LCD pixel aesthetic. Entire image only black segmented shapes on a pale sage-gray screen with a dark sage border, no warm ivory and no 3D sprite shading. Build each fighter from disconnected angular bars like a fixed LCD icon: hexagonal head, trapezoid torso, two bent leg segments. Weapons are large single segmented icons. No faces, clothing or armor details. Six rigid simplified silhouette poses; allies have circular frame bases, foes sawtooth frame bases. The floor is mostly blank with tiny corner ticks, not a bright continuous lattice. Obstacles are simple black-top trapezoid blocks. No texture, gradients, volumetric rendering or typical RPG sprites. Create ONE complete readable tactical fantasy battlefield image, not a sprite sheet or collage. Common comparison scene: an isolated square 8-by-8 board (64 visible cells), shallow isometric view with broad 4:3 diamond tile tops, all edges visible, no perspective vanishing. Three small allied mercenaries occupy the near-left third: shield fighter, longbow archer, dual-dagger rogue. Three hostile fighters occupy the far-right third: broad club wielder, narrow spear wielder, jagged bow wielder. Each figure stands inside ONE cell; weapons and gaps separate silhouettes. Two solid stone blocks interrupt the middle; leave a clear route around them. A single raised floor-spike tile and a separate acid-puddle tile must differ by SHAPE, not only color. One ally has a double-corner selected-cell marker; three empty cells have tiny path dots; one short three-segment health bar is partly empty. Team identity uses round allied bases versus notched hostile bases as well as color. Keep floor calm, characters and hazards highest contrast. No extra actors, mage, scenery, text, numbers, logo, HUD panel, blur, bloom or random pixel noise. 4:3 landscape. Use crisp coarse square pixels throughout.
